features.description: metrics.jsonl rows carry token totals, cache_hit_rate and context_peak read from a real stream-json fixture that the stub replays.
steps: tests/fixtures/usage-tokens.jsonl is a real transcript: `claude -p "<a prompt that writes one small file>" --model haiku --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode auto` run in an empty temp directory (about a cent; the one-time capture the spec asks for, recorded in the D-H34 entry as the exception to build-only). It has at least one `assistant` event with `message.usage` and a `tool_use` block named `Write`, and a `result` event with `usage` and `modelUsage`. Session ids and the temp path may be replaced; no field is invented

lib/metrics.mjs `outcome()` returns tokens_in, cache_read, cache_write, tokens_out (combined over result events the way the plan fixed), cache_hit_rate = cache_read / (tokens_in + cache_read + cache_write) rounded to 3 decimals, and context_peak = the largest `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` of any assistant event; `append` writes them to the metrics row

tests/run.sh check `metrics.mjs: tokens, cache rate and context peak from the real fixture`: a `node --input-type=module -e` import of outcome on tests/fixtures/usage-tokens.jsonl equals the literal numbers the session computed with jq from the fixture (the literals are in the check)

tests/stub-claude.sh `ok()` emits the fixture's assistant and result events (usage kept, cost and result text substituted) so every stub session carries tokens; tests/run.sh check `metrics: coding rows carry tokens, cache rate and context peak` on run demo: `jq -e 'select(.kind=="coding") | .tokens_in > 0 and .cache_hit_rate >= 0 and .cache_hit_rate <= 1 and .context_peak > 0'`
Both checks were watched failing first (FAIL lines quoted in the entry); bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

tests/run.sh check `metrics.mjs: orientation stops at the first Write`: `node --input-type=module -e` on tests/fixtures/usage-tokens.jsonl equals the literal numbers computed by hand from the fixture, and a transcript without edits counts everything
metrics rows gain orient_tokens, orient_turns, orient_s; tests/run.sh check `metrics: orientation recorded per session`: run demo's coding rows have `orient_tokens > 0` and `orient_turns >= 1`
Both checks watched failing first; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

features.description: `harness eval run [--set S] [--harness REF] [--label L]` runs each task of a set with that harness version's driver on a clone with a local bare origin and writes the results under evals/results/.
steps: `harness eval run --set <name or path> --harness <ref> --label <L>` (bin/harness dispatches `eval` to lib/eval.sh): checks the harness repo out at <ref> (default HEAD) into /tmp/harness-eval/<stamp>/harness with `git worktree add`, clones each task's repo at its base into /tmp/harness-eval/<stamp>/<task> with a local bare origin, seeds branch harness/<task-run> with the task's features as feature_list.json, and runs that worktree's bin/harness start --foreground with MERGE_POLICY=off, RETRO=0, no notifications and HARNESS_GH=false

Each task's summary.json, metrics.jsonl, harness-log.md and feature_list.json land in evals/results/<stamp>-<short sha of ref>-<label>/<task>/ and eval.json there records stamp, ref, sha, label, tasks and the clone paths; the harness worktree is removed afterwards (`git worktree list` has no /tmp/harness-eval entry)

tests/run.sh check `eval run: two stub tasks end to end, results in place`: a set of two tasks (written by the test into $T, repo = a throwaway repo with a local bare origin, 1 and 2 features) runs against the stub claude; both summary.json files show every feature passing and the results dir name ends in `-$(git -C $HERE/.. rev-parse --short HEAD)-test`

tests/run.sh check `eval run: --harness <ref> runs that ref's driver`: with `--harness HEAD` the sha in the results dir equals `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, each task's summary.json `harness.version` equals it, and the eval's log names the temp worktree path

tests/run.sh check `eval run: nothing reaches a remote`: the task clones' `git remote get-url origin` paths are under the eval directory, $T/gh.log gained no line during the eval and $T/curl.log gained no post
All three checks watched failing first; bash -n lib/eval.sh; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

features.description: The eval respects EVAL_BUDGET_USD, refuses to start past WEEKLY_STOP_AT, and `--repeat N` runs each task N times.
steps: lib/config.sh has `EVAL_BUDGET_USD=10` among the defaults; after each task the eval sums the tasks' summary.json costs and starts no further task once the sum is at or over the cap, printing and writing in eval.json `budget: $<spent> of $<cap>; <n> tasks not started`
tests/run.sh check `eval: the budget cap stops starting tasks`: EVAL_BUDGET_USD=0.3 with the stub (a session costs $0.25) runs the first task only and eval.json names the second as not started

Before starting, the eval reads `$HARNESS_STATE/USAGE_7D` (the real state root outside tests) with `weekly_over` and exits 1 with the window's message when it is past WEEKLY_STOP_AT; tests/run.sh check `eval: refuses past WEEKLY_STOP_AT`: with USAGE_7D `0.9 <epoch an hour ahead>` the eval exits 1, prints `7-day window at 90%` and creates no results dir
`--repeat N` runs each task N times into <task>/r1 … <task>/rN with fresh clones; tests/run.sh check `eval: --repeat 2 runs each task twice`: both r1 and r2 summary.json files exist for each task
All three checks watched failing first; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

features.description: `harness eval compare <A> <B>` prints a per-task and total table of pass rate, $ and tokens per verified feature, cache hit rate, orientation, context peak, wall time and rework with a verdict per metric.
steps: lib/eval.mjs exports pure `compare(a, b)` taking two loaded result sets and returning rows { task, metric, a, b, verdict } where verdict is `better`, `worse`, `within noise` or `one sample`; noise is the spread (max − min) across a task's repeats, pass rate is pass^N over the repeats, and the totals row aggregates every task

tests/run.sh check `eval.mjs: compare verdicts`: a `node --input-type=module -e` case with two repeats each gives `within noise` when the difference is inside the spread, `better` or `worse` when outside (direction right for cost, which is better when lower, and for pass rate, which is better when higher), and `one sample` with a single repeat

`harness eval compare <resultA> <resultB>` prints a markdown table with one line per task and metric and a totals block, then one line per metric with its verdict; tests/run.sh check `eval compare prints the table`: comparing the two test results shows a `pass rate` line and a verdict for each of the eight metrics
Both checks watched failing first; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

features.description: `harness eval probes <task-result>` derives handoff questions from a finished task's record, asks one Haiku session that sees only the next coding session's prompt, and scores the answers by match.
steps: lib/eval.sh `probes <task result dir>` derives at least three question kinds from the record with their answers from git and the feature list: which files <feature> changed (paths of the commits whose subject starts `<feature>:` in the task's clone, named in eval.json), what <feature> depends on (its `after` or the features before it), and what the last attempt at <feature> failed on (the final text of its last non-passing metrics row); questions and answers are written to probes.json

It renders the coding prompt the next session would get for the task's next feature (the same render.mjs call and extras as lib/driver.sh prompt(); from E4 on, with context.md) and asks one Haiku session with that prompt plus the questions, no tools (`--max-turns 1` and `--permission-mode dontAsk` with an empty allow list), so the model sees only the handoff context; the prompt's first line is `# Probe session`
Each answer is scored exact (1) or contains (1) or miss (0); the command prints one line per question and `score <n>/<m>` and stores it in probes.json

tests/stub-claude.sh answers a `# Probe session` prompt with a fixed result text that gets one question right and one wrong; tests/run.sh check `eval probes: questions derived, answers scored` runs probes on a test result and sees `score 1/2` and at least two questions in probes.json, watched failing first
bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

steps: docs/plans/2026-10-21-E4-memory.md exists, first line `Milestone base: <sha>`, with: the entry JSON schema (feature, kind, outcome, summary ≤ 400 chars, files, verified_how, tests_before, tests_after, dead_ends, discoveries with affects, questions, proposed_changes, evidence rows for verify) and the stamped fields (at, session, model); the lib/entries.mjs API (validate, minimal, render, pack, CLI verbs); the exact driver points (after the `WIP` commit of a coding session and before `F repair`; in verify() after `restrict` and before the `before` count and `F evidence`, which keep reading the rendered progress.md); how the initializer's entry works (it writes entry.json too; the driver renders the header); the rendered shapes (progress.md: header, 15 newest in full with the verify table in the five-column shape features.mjs counts, then one line per older entry linking to progress-archive.md; the archive complete); the context pack algorithm (priority order, CONTEXT_PACK_BYTES default 8192 in lib/config.sh, the `→ entries.jsonl:<line>` reference per item); the legacy rule (a run whose feature list exists and has no entries.jsonl is left alone by the renderer; `harness continue` on it moves progress.md to progress-archive.md and starts the journal, noting it); the stub changes (entry.json per coding and verify session, STUB_BAD_ENTRY, a dead end for C's first attempt); the checks per feature; D-H39 (journal, single writer), D-H40 (rendered progress), D-H41 (context pack) or the next free numbers

features.description: lib/entries.mjs holds the pure rules: validating an entry, building a minimal one, and rendering progress.md and progress-archive.md from a list of entries.
steps: lib/entries.mjs (one-line usage header, exported functions, no dependencies) has `validate(obj)` → errors (empty when valid), `minimal({ feature, kind, outcome, files, final })`, `renderProgress(entries, { full: 15, header })` and `renderArchive(entries, header)`

tests/run.sh check `entries.mjs: validate accepts the schema and names what is wrong`: a full valid entry gives no errors; a summary of 401 characters, a missing outcome and an outcome outside passes · not yet · parked each give an error naming the field

tests/run.sh check `entries.mjs: progress renders 15 in full and the rest as archive lines`: 20 entries render 15 `### ` headers newest first, then 5 one-line items each linking `progress-archive.md`; a verify entry renders the `| Feature | Step | ... | Holds |` table so that features.mjs `evidence` counts its rows; the archive holds all 20 in full
Both checks watched failing first; node --check lib/entries.mjs; no driver change in this feature; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

features.description: Sessions write entry.json; the driver, the single writer, validates it, stamps it, appends it to entries.jsonl and deletes it, recording a minimal entry when it is missing or malformed.
steps: After every coding, verify and initializer session lib/driver.sh reads <run>/entry.json, validates it with lib/entries.mjs, stamps at, session (the transcript name) and model, appends one line to <run>/entries.jsonl and deletes entry.json; a missing or invalid file gets a `note` (`<id>: entry.json missing|invalid (<first error>); recorded a minimal entry`) and a minimal entry built from the files changed since the session's start commit and the session's final message

prompts/coding.md, verify.md and initializer.md tell the session to write <run>/entry.json in the plan's schema (shown in the prompt) before finishing; in this feature they still write their progress.md entry as before

tests/stub-claude.sh writes entry.json for coding and verify sessions (verify with evidence rows; C's first attempt with a dead end `left BROKEN in the tree`); STUB_BAD_ENTRY=<id> writes `{not json` for that id's first session

tests/run.sh check `entries: the driver appends each session's entry`: run demo's entries.jsonl has one line per coding and verify session, each with at, session, model and feature, and no entry.json is left in the run dir; check `a malformed entry is recorded as minimal and the run goes on`: with STUB_BAD_ENTRY=B harness-log.md has the note and B's first entry has outcome from its passes and files from git, and the run still ends `done`
Both checks watched failing first; journal/decisions.md has D-H39; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

features.description: progress.md and progress-archive.md are rendered by the driver from entries.jsonl after every session; sessions stop writing progress.md; legacy runs are untouched until continued.
steps: lib/driver.sh regenerates <run>/progress.md and <run>/progress-archive.md from entries.jsonl right after each append (initializer, coding, verify), and verify's `before` count and `F evidence` read the rendered file; prompts/coding.md, verify.md and initializer.md no longer ask for a progress.md entry (the initializer writes its header text into its entry); the stub stops writing progress.md

tests/run.sh check `progress.md is rendered from the journal`: in run demo the `### ` headers of progress.md equal entries.jsonl's entries newest first, the verify M1 entry shows its evidence table, and the existing verify checks (`verifier caught A, re-queued`, `thin verify evidence`) still pass on the rendered file

Legacy: a run whose feature list exists without entries.jsonl is neither rendered nor ingested (its sessions' progress.md edits stand); `harness continue` on it copies progress.md to progress-archive.md, starts entries.jsonl and notes `journal started; progress.md kept as progress-archive.md`. tests/run.sh check `a legacy run is untouched, then continued into a journal`: run 14's record (legacy) before continue has no entries.jsonl and its progress.md is unchanged by the start-up; after `harness continue legacy` progress-archive.md equals the old progress.md byte for byte and entries.jsonl exists
Both checks watched failing first; journal/decisions.md has D-H40; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing

features.description: Before each session the driver writes <run>/context.md, a deterministic context pack capped by CONTEXT_PACK_BYTES in a fixed priority order, and the prompts say to read it first.
steps: lib/entries.mjs exports pure `pack(entries, { feature, list, answers, cap })` returning markdown ≤ cap bytes built in this order: this feature's earlier attempts, dead ends and questions; the INBOX answers; discoveries whose affects names this feature or `run`; the latest entry of each feature in its `after`; the last 3 entries of the run; each item ends with `→ entries.jsonl:<line>`; lib/config.sh has `CONTEXT_PACK_BYTES=8192`

tests/run.sh check `entries.mjs: the pack keeps a feature's dead end under a flood and respects the cap`: 200 unrelated entries of 300 bytes plus one earlier attempt of feature X with a dead end give a pack ≤ 8192 bytes whose first item is X's dead end, with the INBOX answers before any discovery and the `→ entries.jsonl:` references present

lib/driver.sh writes <run>/context.md before every coding and verify session (committed with the run record); prompts/coding.md and verify.md open their bearings section with `Read context.md first; the full record is entries.jsonl / progress-archive.md`; tests/run.sh check `context.md carries the earlier attempt's dead end`: the context.md saved before C's second session in run demo contains `left BROKEN in the tree` and prompt-coding.md names context.md
Both checks watched failing first; journal/decisions.md has D-H41; bash tests/run.sh ends with every check passing
